facts.raw_span: Serological tests for amoebiasis and hydatid disease were negative
a 11 × 7.5 × 11.2 cm predominantly anechoic, thick-walled lesion arising from the inferior surface of the liver
low-level internal echoes and a homogeneous echogenic area in its superolateral portion
the gallbladder was not visualized separately

concepts.why: The patient presented with hepatomegaly, tenderness in the right hypochondrium, and a thick-walled lesion arising from the liver, which is consistent with a liver abscess.

The patient had a predominantly anechoic, thick-walled lesion arising from the liver, with low-level internal echoes and a homogeneous echogenic area, which is consistent with an infected non-parasitic cyst.
The patient presented with hepatomegaly, a thick-walled lesion arising from the liver, and turbid fluid, which is consistent with a hepatic cyst infection.
The patient had a thick-walled lesion arising from the liver, with low-level internal echoes and a homogeneous echogenic area, which is consistent with a pyogenic liver cyst.
The patient had a predominantly anechoic, thick-walled lesion arising from the liver, which is consistent with a solitary liver cyst.
It explains the negative serological tests for amoebiasis and hydatid disease, indicating the liver cyst infection is not due to these parasitic causes.

rationales.F01: Right upper abdominal discomfort is a common symptom of liver abscess and other liver conditions.
rationales.F03: Low-grade fever is a common symptom of infected liver conditions.
rationales.F05: Hepatomegaly is a common sign of liver abscess and other liver conditions.
rationales.F08: Negative serological tests for amoebiasis and hydatid disease rule out these conditions.
rationales.F09: The presence of a large, thick-walled lesion arising from the liver is highly suggestive of a liver abscess or infected cyst.
rationales.F10: Low-level internal echoes and a homogeneous echogenic area are consistent with an infected liver lesion.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's presentation with a thick-walled, anechoic lesion and turbid fluid, along with the lack of jaundice and normal liver function tests, supports the diagnosis of an infected non-parasitic cyst, which is further confirmed by the contrast-enhanced CT findings of a well-defined, lobulated cystic lesion with a solid component.
